title: From 46% to 90%: Fine-Tuning Tiny LLMs for On-Device Agents — Cormac Brick, Google

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 66%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on LiteRT-LM as an on-device inference runtime, covering quantization, NPU acceleration, the PyTorch-to-LiteRT-LM deployment workflow, and tokens-per-second performance metrics for serving models on edge devices. The talk presents developer platforms (LiteRT-LM, AI Core, AI Edge Gallery, skill creation tooling) for building on-device AI with cross-domain applicability across consumer and enterprise use cases. The talk covers deployment via the export-and-inference workflow, production use through the Eloquent app and on-device performance benchmarks, and evaluation of Function Gemma accuracy before and after fine-tuning. Requires familiarity with mobile app development, LLM concepts, function calling, and PyTorch model export workflows. Claims are supported by live demos, quantitative performance data, and a shipping production app, though without rigorous comparative studies.

summary:
Cormac Brick introduces two paths for on-device AI. System-level GenAI uses Gemini Nano via AI Core, pre-installed in the OS with Gemma 4 E2B and E4B as base models, offering optimized, preloaded capabilities that don't increase app size. App-level GenAI uses LiteRT-LM runtime for custom models shipped within apps, providing greater customization and cross-platform reach but requiring more developer effort. The LiteRT runtime (formerly TensorFlow Lite) supports over 2.7 billion devices with CPU, GPU, and NPU execution options.

The Google AI Edge Gallery app demonstrates these capabilities on iOS and Android, supporting AI chat, image queries, audio scribing, and custom skills. Agent skills built on Gemma 4 use a skill harness with system prompts, a load_skill tool call for on-demand loading, and a show_JS tool for rendering JavaScript UI. Developers can create skills using Gemini CLI, publish to GitHub, and load via URL; the community built approximately 80 skills in the first week.

For tiny models (100-200M parameters), fine-tuning with synthetic data is often needed. Function Gemma, a 270M parameter model based on Gemma 3 technology, achieves robust function calling when fine-tuned. Out of the box it hit 46% accuracy on app intents; after synthetic-data fine-tuning using Flash, it cleared over 90% on eight of ten functions. A Hugging Face space fine-tuning lab is available. The export workflow goes from PyTorch through LiteRT-Torch to LiteRT-LM single-file format, which replaces .task files for LLMs. Apple's fast VLM (500M parameters) runs on Qualcomm NPU through this stack.

Eloquent, a production iOS transcription app, chains two tiny Gemma 3-based models: an ASR engine and a text polishing engine, each a few hundred million parameters. It supports personalization with custom keywords and removes filler words, demonstrating that fine-tuned tiny LLMs work in production. Q&A revealed that multi-skill calling within a single answer is still being improved, and performance data on CPU/TPU is available in a separate talk and the Gemma LiteRT-LM model card.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and overview of on-device agents and tiny LLMs
sections.summary: Speaker introduces the talk covering agent skills on device and tiny LLMs (under 1B parameters), built on a skill harness on top of AI Core. Outlines the agenda: AI Edge SLMs/TLMs, agent skills, and tiny models.

sections.title: AI Edge stack: SLMs, TLMs, and system vs app-level GenAI
sections.summary: Covers motivations for on-device AI (latency, privacy, offline, reliability, savings). Introduces AI Edge stack: MediaPipe, LiteRT-LM, and LiteRT runtime (formerly TensorFlow Lite) supporting CPU/GPU/NPU across 2.7B+ devices. Contrasts system-level GenAI (Gemini Nano via AI Core, Gemma 4 E2B/E4B base models, preloaded, no app size increase) with app-level GenAI (LiteRT-LM, custom models shipped with app, more work but full customization).

sections.title: Google AI Edge Gallery app demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates the Google AI Edge Gallery app on iOS and Android for running LLMs locally. App supports AI chat, image queries, audio scribe, custom skills, and 3P models. Uses AI Core when available. Open source on Android with iOS planned. Shows restaurant roulette demo built on Gemma 4 with a simple agent harness.

sections.title: Agent skills and skill harness architecture
sections.summary: Explains how the skill harness works: system prompts include skill descriptions, a load_skill tool call loads skills on demand, and a show_JS tool renders JavaScript UI in-app. Restaurant roulette used custom JavaScript for the roulette wheel rendering. Skills are loaded selectively so the model doesn't see all function details upfront.

sections.title: Creating and publishing custom skills
sections.summary: Covers skill creation via hand-writing or using Gemini CLI/code coach to generate skills from prompts. Skills can be published to GitHub and loaded via URL in the app. Team built ~80 skills. Community has shared example skills since launch. An ADB skill enables device debugging and testing.

sections.title: LiteRT-LM runtime for model deployment
sections.summary: LiteRT-LM is the runtime for running models in a single-file format packaging everything needed for inference. Open source, fast, cross-platform. C++ and Java APIs available now; Swift and JavaScript APIs coming soon. Supports Gemma 4 across devices. iOS app open-sourcing planned with Swift API release.

sections.title: Export and inference workflow for tiny models
sections.summary: Deployment workflow: start from transformers, use LiteRT-Torch to export, deploy with LiteRT-LM. Demo shows quant 0.6 model running on desktop with GPU, and Apple's fast VLM (500M params) running on Qualcomm NPU with hardware acceleration. For smaller models (100-200M params), developers use pre-built fixed-function models or fine-tune models.

sections.title: Function Gemma: fine-tuning tiny models with synthetic data
sections.summary: Function Gemma is a 270M parameter model based on Gemma 3 technology published last December, enabling robust function calling. Runs nearly 2,000 tokens/sec prefill and 140 decode on Pixel 7. Out of the box it achieved 46% accuracy on app intents; after synthetic-data fine-tuning using Flash to generate a dataset, it reached over 90% on eight of ten functions. A Hugging Face space fine-tuning lab is available for developers to define functions, upload data, and fine-tune. This workflow is more effort than prompting a larger model but enables robust, reliable function calling at scale in apps.

sections.title: Eloquent: production transcription app using chained tiny models
sections.summary: Eloquent is a transcription app (iOS only, not yet in Europe) built using two chained tiny Gemma 3-based models: an ASR engine and a text polishing engine, each a few hundred million parameters. Supports personalization with custom keywords and removes filler words. Serves as a proof-of-life example that fine-tuned tiny LLMs work in production for compelling offline experiences.

sections.title: Q&A: Agent skill robustness, file format, and performance
sections.summary: Q&A covers: the 4B parameter Gemma 4 model handles about 8 skills by default and sequential skill calling within a conversation works well, but calling multiple skills in a single answer is still being improved. LiteRT-LM file format replaces .task files for LLMs (bundling tokenizer and model), while .task files remain for non-LLM tasks. Performance data on CPU/TPU is available in a separate talk and the Gemma LiteRT-LM model card.
